root_cause_label: Knowledge gap on C++11 constexpr restrictions combined with false confirmation from own runtime test
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent incorrectly concluded the existing constexpr implementation was already C++11 compatible based on runtime compilation alone, then made the wrong fix (removing constexpr) rather than rewriting the function body to be C++11-compliant, causing the benchmark's compile-time tests to fail.
t_err_evidence: At step 2 (think), the agent concludes 'The current implementation appears to already be C++11 compatible' after reviewing the header, failing to recognize that C++11 constexpr functions cannot contain loops or mutable local variables like the existing implementation does.
t_commit_evidence: At step 10, the agent successfully removes the constexpr keyword from sum_array.h (after a failed attempt at step 9), permanently breaking the compile-time interface that the benchmark tests require via static_assert-style usage.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the knowledge that C++11 constexpr functions cannot contain loops or mutable local variables (those are C++14 relaxations). This causes it to incorrectly assess the existing implementation as already C++11 compatible. It further compounds this by designing its own test that only validates runtime compilation, not compile-time constexpr evaluation, treating a passing runtime test as proof of full C++11 compatibility.
forewarning_evidence: At step 9, the str_replace edit command fails with 'ERROR: No replacement was performed, old_str did not appear verbatim in /app/sum_array.h', signaling the agent's edit strategy had problems before the actual wrong fix was applied at step 10.
